scenes.title: Hallucination vs. Ungrounded: A Crucial Distinction
scenes.teaching_intent: To clarify the difference between an LLM hallucinating and an answer being ungrounded, and why this distinction is vital for RAG system evaluation.
scenes.necessity: When an LLM produces incorrect information, it's important to understand *how* it's incorrect. For RAG systems, a factually true answer can still be problematic if it didn't come from the provided sources, breaking the 'trust contract'.
scenes.story: Imagine you're a lawyer, and you've asked your assistant to summarize a legal document, providing only facts from that document. Now, your assistant gives you a 'fact'. What if that fact is completely made up? That's one problem. But what if the fact is actually true in the real world, but it wasn't mentioned *anywhere* in the document you gave them? That's a different kind of problem, right? You specifically asked for information *from the document*.
scenes.narration:
Hallucination और Ungrounded Answer में क्या नाजुक फर्क है?
ये बहुत जरूरी फर्क है दोस्त! सोचो यूजर ने पूछा 'भारत की राजधानी क्या है?' और दिए गए डॉक्यूमेंट में सिर्फ फ्रांस और पेरिस के बारे में लिखा था।
अब अगर मॉडल कहे 'भारत की राजधानी नई दिल्ली है' तब?
तो ये जवाब दुनिया के हिसाब से 100% सच है, लेकिन RAG के संदर्भ में Ungrounded है! क्योंकि ये बात उस डॉक्यूमेंट में नहीं लिखी थी।
और Hallucination क्या है?
जब वो कहे 'भारत की राजधानी पेरिस है'! ये दुनिया के हिसाब से भी झूठ है और डॉक्यूमेंट के हिसाब से भी। RAG इवैल्यूएशन में दोनों को अलग-अलग नापना पड़ता है!
scenes.question: This subtle but important difference is key for evaluating RAG systems. So, what's the difference between hallucination and a factually correct but ungrounded/unsupported answer — and why does the distinction matter for evaluation?

The distinction matters because a RAG system is supposed to answer from the provided sources; an ungrounded-but-true answer still breaks the trust/citation contract of the system. Faithfulness evaluation specifically measures groundedness against the retrieved context, independent of whether the claim happens to be true in the real world — this is why faithfulness and correctness are tracked as separate metrics in rigorous RAG evaluation.

scenes.title: Red-teaming: Proactively Breaking LLM Applications
scenes.teaching_intent: To explain the adversarial nature of red-teaming and differentiate it from standard QA, emphasizing its role in finding vulnerabilities.
scenes.necessity: LLMs can be exploited or made to misbehave in unexpected ways by clever users. Standard QA testing, which focuses on expected inputs, isn't enough to uncover these adversarial vulnerabilities.
scenes.story: Imagine you've built a fortress. Standard QA is like checking if all the doors lock and the walls are sturdy. But 'red-teaming' is hiring a team of professional ethical hackers whose *only job* is to find every single way to break into that fortress – through hidden tunnels, exploiting weak points, or even tricking guards. They're trying to *break* the system, not just confirm it works.
scenes.narration:
Red-Teaming क्या होता है? क्या हम खुद अपनी ही ऐप को हैक करने की कोशिश करते हैं?
बिल्कुल दोस्त! अपनी ऐप को दुनिया के सामने लॉन्च करने से पहले, हम अपनी एक टीम को 'शैतान' बनने को कहते हैं!
शैतान मतलब?
उनका काम ही होता है ऐप को तोड़ना! वो उल्टे-सीधे सवाल पूछेंगे, जेलब्रेक ट्राय करेंगे, बॉट को भड़काने की कोशिश करेंगे ताकि उसकी कमजोरियां सामने आ जाएं।
और जो कमजोरियां मिलें, उन्हें ठीक कर लो!
हाँ! इससे पहले कि कोई असली हैकर तुम्हारी ऐप को बदनाम करे, तुम खुद उसकी सारी कमियां ढूंढकर सील कर देते हो।
scenes.question: This proactive, adversarial approach is crucial for LLM safety. So, what does red-teaming an LLM application actually involve, and how is it different from standard QA testing?
scenes.interview_question: This proactive, adversarial approach is crucial for LLM safety. So, what does red-teaming an LLM application actually involve, and how is it different from standard QA testing?
scenes.interview_view:
Standard QA tests whether the system works correctly on expected inputs. Red-teaming deliberately searches for inputs that make the system fail or misbehave — adversarial prompts designed to elicit jailbreaks, harmful content, prompt injection success, PII leakage, or policy violations — treating the system as a target to break rather than a spec to confirm. It combines manual adversarial testing by people trained to think like an attacker, automated adversarial prompt generation/fuzzing, and testing across known jailbreak patterns and domain-specific edge cases. The output of red-teaming should feed back into guardrails, system prompt hardening, and the evaluation suite, turning findings into permanent regression tests.

scenes.title: Evaluating LLM Applications for Bias and Fairness
scenes.teaching_intent: To explain the complexities of evaluating LLMs for bias and fairness, emphasizing the need for targeted evaluation sets and a continuous process.
scenes.necessity: LLMs learn from vast datasets that often reflect societal biases. If unchecked, an LLM application can perpetuate or even amplify these biases, leading to unfair or discriminatory outcomes for certain demographic groups.
scenes.story: Imagine you're developing an AI system to help with hiring decisions, like screening resumes. If this system, even unintentionally, starts systematically favoring candidates with certain names or from specific backgrounds, even when their qualifications are identical, that's a huge problem, right? It's not just about overall accuracy; it's about equitable treatment for everyone.
scenes.narration:
AI में Bias और Fairness कैसे टेस्ट करते हैं?
दोस्त, AI इंसानों के लिखे इंटरनेट डेटा से सीखता है, और इंसानों में बहुत सारे पूर्वाग्रह होते हैं! जैसे जेंडर, जाति या धर्म को लेकर।
तो मॉडल भी पक्षपाती बन सकता है?
हाँ! जैसे अगर तुम प्रॉम्प्ट दो 'डॉक्टर ने नर्स से बात की' तो वो डॉक्टर को 'He' और नर्स को 'She' मान सकता है।
इसे कैसे सुधारें?

scenes.title: Understanding the Bias-Variance Tradeoff
scenes.teaching_intent: To explain the fundamental bias-variance tradeoff in machine learning and how to diagnose overfitting and underfitting.
scenes.necessity: A core challenge in machine learning is building models that generalize well to new, unseen data. Understanding bias and variance helps us diagnose why a model might not be generalizing and how to fix it.
scenes.story: Imagine you're trying to teach a student to recognize different animals. One student is very simplistic: they learn that 'all animals have four legs' (high bias). They'll misclassify birds and snakes. Another student memorizes *every single detail* of every animal photo you show them, including the background color and lighting (high variance). They'll be great at identifying *those specific photos*, but terrible at recognizing the same animals in new photos or different settings.
scenes.narration:
मशीन लर्निंग का सबसे मशहूर नियम — Bias-Variance Tradeoff क्या है?
इसे तीरंदाजी से समझो दोस्त! अगर तुम्हारे सारे तीर निशाने से बहुत दूर गिर रहे हैं, लेकिन सब एक ही जगह गिर रहे हैं — तो ये High Bias यानी Underfitting है। मॉडल बहुत भोला है, कुछ सीख ही नहीं पाया।
और अगर तीर निशाने के आसपास इधर-उधर बिखर रहे हैं?
तो वो High Variance यानी Overfitting है! उसने ट्रेनिंग डेटा के सारे शोर और कमियों को रट लिया है, लेकिन नई चीजों पर लड़खड़ा रहा है।
तो हमें क्या चाहिए?
हमें चाहिए Low Bias और Low Variance — यानी तीर बिल्कुल निशाने के बीचों-बीच लगे! मॉडल न बहुत सीधा हो और न रट्टू तोता।
scenes.question: Both students fail to generalize well, but for different reasons. This dilemma is at the heart of machine learning, leading to the question: Explain the bias-variance tradeoff. How do you diagnose whether a model is overfitting or underfitting?
scenes.interview_question: Both students fail to generalize well, but for different reasons. This dilemma is at the heart of machine learning, leading to the question: Explain the bias-variance tradeoff. How do you diagnose whether a model is overfitting or underfitting?
scenes.interview_view:
Bias is error from overly simplistic assumptions (the model can't capture the true pattern even with unlimited data); variance is error from being overly sensitive to the specific training set (the model captures noise, not just signal). Total generalization error decomposes roughly into bias² + variance + irreducible noise, and the two typically trade off against each other as model complexity changes. Underfitting (high bias) shows up as poor performance on both training and validation/test data. Overfitting (high variance) shows up as strong training performance but a large, widening gap to validation/test performance. Diagnosis in practice: plot training vs. validation loss curves; a widening gap is the classic overfitting signature. Fixes for overfitting include more data, regularization (dropout, weight decay, early stopping), or a simpler model; fixes for underfitting include a more expressive model, more training time, or better features.

scenes.title: Backpropagation and Optimizers (SGD, Momentum, Adam)
scenes.teaching_intent: To explain the mechanism of backpropagation for training deep networks and differentiate common optimization algorithms.
scenes.necessity: Deep learning models have millions or billions of parameters. An efficient method is needed to calculate how each parameter contributes to the overall error (loss) so the model can learn and improve.
scenes.story: Imagine you're trying to find the lowest point in a vast, complex mountain range, but you're blindfolded. You can only feel the slope directly beneath your feet to decide which direction to take a small step. If you take a step and realize you went uphill, you know you need to adjust. Now, imagine doing this for a million different 'feet' all at once, each influencing the others. That's the challenge of training a deep neural network.
scenes.narration:
Backpropagation और Optimizers (SGD, Adam) — AI का दिमाग कैसे सुधरता है?
सोचो तुम आंख बंद करके किसी पहाड़ी से नीचे उतर रही हो। तुम अपने पैरों से ढलान महसूस करती हो और नीचे की तरफ कदम बढ़ाती हो।
हाँ, जिधर ढलान नीचे हो, उधर ही चलूंगी।
Gradient Descent यही करता है! Backpropagation बताता है कि गलती किस न्यूरॉन की वजह से हुई (ढलान किधर है)। और Adam Optimizer तय करता है कि कदम कितना बड़ा और तेज रखना है।
ताकि हम जल्दी से सबसे निचले गड्ढे यानी मिनिमम एरर तक पहुंच सकें?
बिल्कुल! Adam स्पीड और मोमेंटम दोनों को संभालता है, इसीलिए हर मॉडर्न डीप लर्निंग मॉडल में AdamW यूज़ होता है।
scenes.question: So, how do deep learning models efficiently figure out how to adjust their parameters to minimize error, and what are the different strategies for taking those 'steps'? This is the essence of: What is backpropagation, and how do optimizers like SGD, Momentum, and Adam differ?
scenes.interview_question: So, how do deep learning models efficiently figure out how to adjust their parameters to minimize error, and what are the different strategies for taking those 'steps'? This is the essence of: What is backpropagation, and how do optimizers like SGD, Momentum, and Adam differ?
scenes.interview_view:
Backpropagation computes the gradient of the loss with respect to every parameter in the network by applying the chain rule backward through the computational graph, layer by layer — this makes training deep networks tractable. Plain SGD updates each parameter directly opposite its gradient, scaled by a learning rate, but can be slow and oscillate. Momentum adds a running average of past gradients to the update, accelerating progress in consistent directions and dampening oscillation. Adam combines momentum with an adaptive, per-parameter learning rate derived from a running average of squared gradients. This adaptivity is why Adam (and variants like AdamW) is the default optimizer for most modern deep learning models, including LLMs.

scenes.title: Diffusion Models vs. GANs for Image Generation
scenes.teaching_intent: To explain the structural differences between diffusion models and GANs and why diffusion became the leading approach for generative media.
scenes.necessity: Understanding how generative image models operate under the hood is critical as GenAI expands beyond text into multimodal applications.
scenes.story: Imagine creating a masterpiece. Option one: a harsh critic standing over your shoulder immediately rejecting every sketch you make until you trick them. Option two: starting with a canvas covered in pure static noise, and gradually, step-by-step, removing tiny bits of noise until a sharp image appears.
scenes.narration:
Diffusion Models vs GANs — Midjourney और DALL-E इतनी खूबसूरत तस्वीरें कैसे बनाते हैं?
पहले GANs चलते थे दोस्त — जहाँ दो नेटवर्क आपस में लड़ते थे (एक चोर और एक पुलिस)। लेकिन वो बहुत नखरे दिखाते थे और कभी-कभी ट्रेनिंग क्रैश हो जाती थी।
फिर Diffusion Models कैसे आए?
Diffusion मॉडल बहुत सब्र वाले हैं! वो पहले एक साफ फोटो में धीरे-धीरे नमक जैसा शोर (Noise) मिलाते हैं जब तक वो पूरा सफेद शोर न बन जाए।
और फिर?
फिर वो उल्टा सीखते हैं — उस शोर में से धीरे-धीरे कचरा हटाकर वापस सुंदर फोटो बनाना! ये स्टेप-बाय-स्टेप डी-नॉइजिंग इतनी कमाल की है कि आज की सारी AI इमेज और वीडियो इसी से बनते हैं।
scenes.question: What is the structural difference between diffusion models and GANs for image generation?
scenes.interview_question: What is the structural difference between diffusion models and GANs for image generation?
scenes.interview_view:
GANs use an adversarial game between a Generator and Discriminator, which is fast at inference but notoriously unstable to train due to mode collapse and vanishing gradients. Diffusion models (like Stable Diffusion and FLUX) work by iteratively denoising a Gaussian noise vector over multiple steps using a UNet or DiT backbone. Training is stable because it simply predicts the noise added at each timestep (MSE loss), though inference requires multiple denoising steps.

scenes.title: Visual Tokenization: How Multimodal LLMs See Images
scenes.teaching_intent: To explain how vision transformers and patch projection convert raw image pixels into tokens compatible with LLM attention blocks.
scenes.necessity: LLMs operate on discrete sequence tokens. To process images alongside text, visual pixels must be transformed into embedding vectors of the same dimension.
scenes.story: Think of a giant jigsaw puzzle. If you want a language model to read a picture, you can't feed it raw RGB matrix values all at once. You chop the picture into a grid of small square patches, flatten each patch into a vector, and treat every patch as if it were a word token in a sentence.
scenes.narration:
Multimodal LLMs (जैसे GPT-4o) तस्वीरों को कैसे देखते हैं? क्या उन्हें आँखें मिल गई हैं?
नहीं दोस्त, उन्हें तो सिर्फ टोकन्स समझ आते हैं! इसलिए तस्वीरों के साथ Visual Tokenization किया जाता है।
ये कैसे होता है?
जैसे हम वाक्य को शब्दों में काटते हैं, वैसे ही Vision Transformer (ViT) फोटो को 16x16 पिक्सल के छोटे-छोटे चौकोर ग्रिड टुकड़ों में काट देता है।
और हर टुकड़े को एक शब्द की तरह ट्रीट करता है?
हाँ! हर टुकड़े का एक वेक्टर बनता है और वो टेक्स्ट टोकन्स के साथ ही मॉडल के दिमाग में घुस जाता है। मॉडल के लिए फोटो भी शब्दों की एक किताब बन जाती है!
scenes.question: How are images tokenized or represented as inputs to a multimodal LLM?
scenes.interview_question: How are images tokenized or represented as inputs to a multimodal LLM?
scenes.interview_view:
Multimodal LLMs (like LLaVA and GPT-4V) use Vision Transformers (ViT) or CLIP vision encoders. The input image is split into non-overlapping patches (e.g., 14x14 pixels), flattened, and linearly projected into visual embedding tokens. A projection layer (linear or MLP) aligns these visual embeddings into the LLM's text embedding space, allowing the LLM decoder to treat image patches as prefix tokens.

scenes.title: Evaluating Image Quality: FID Score and CLIP Score
scenes.teaching_intent: To clarify quantitative metrics for evaluating synthetic image quality and text-image alignment.
scenes.necessity: Unlike text where BLEU or RAGAS evaluate tokens, image generation requires metrics for both visual realism and prompt fidelity.
scenes.story: If an AI generates a photo of a 'cyberpunk cat riding a skateboard', how do you measure if it looks like a real photo versus a blurry mess, and whether the cat is actually on a skateboard?
scenes.narration:
AI की बनाई फोटो कितनी अच्छी है, ये कैसे नापते हैं? FID और CLIP स्कोर क्या हैं?
इंसान तो कह देगा 'वाह, क्या सुंदर फोटो है!' लेकिन कंप्यूटर कैसे नापेगा? इसके लिए दो स्कोर हैं दोस्त: पहला FID Score (Fréchet Inception Distance)।
ये क्या देखता है?
ये देखता है कि असली दुनिया की तस्वीरों और AI की बनाई तस्वीरों के डिस्ट्रीब्यूशन में कितनी दूरी है। FID स्कोर जितना कम होगा, फोटो उतनी ही ज्यादा असली और रियलिस्टिक होगी!
और CLIP Score?
CLIP Score देखता है कि जो प्रॉम्प्ट तुमने दिया था (जैसे 'लाल टोपी वाला बिल्ली'), क्या फोटो वाकई उसी प्रॉम्प्ट से मैच करती है या कुछ और ही बन गया!

scenes.title: Serverless GPU vs. Dedicated GPU Instances for LLMs
scenes.teaching_intent: To guide architectural decisions between serverless cold-start inference and dedicated GPU compute instances.
scenes.necessity: GPU instance costs are high. Deciding when to use serverless providers vs. self-hosted GPU clusters impacts unit economics.
scenes.story: Imagine running a taxi service. Option A: buying and parking 5 expensive sports cars in a garage 24/7, paying rent even when no passengers call. Option B: calling a rideshare driver whenever a passenger appears, but waiting 30 seconds for them to arrive.
scenes.narration:
Serverless GPU vs Dedicated GPU — अपनी AI ऐप के लिए क्या रेंट पर लें?
दोस्त, अगर तुम्हारी ऐप अभी नई है, दिन में सिर्फ 500 यूजर आते हैं और रात में सब सो जाते हैं — तो Serverless GPU (जैसे Modal, RunPod) चुनो!
क्योंकि इसमें सिर्फ चले हुए सेकंड्स का पैसा लगता है?
बिल्कुल! जब रिक्वेस्ट आएगी, तभी GPU जगेगा, बाकी समय 0 रुपये का बिल। लेकिन अगर तुम्हारी ऐप पर 24 घंटे लगातार ट्रैफिक रहता है, तो Dedicated GPU ले लो। वो भारी ट्रैफिक में ज्यादा सस्ता और बिना कोल्ड-स्टार्ट के चलेगा।
scenes.question: Serverless GPU inference vs. always-on dedicated servers — how do you decide?
scenes.interview_question: Serverless GPU inference vs. always-on dedicated servers — how do you decide?
scenes.interview_view:

Always-on dedicated GPU instances (e.g., AWS g5/p4, RunPod, Lambda Labs) running engines like vLLM or TensorRT-LLM provide minimal latency and lower cost at high, steady request volumes.

scenes.title: Load Balancing & Multi-Provider Failover Architecture
scenes.teaching_intent: To explain resilience patterns for routing LLM traffic across multiple instances and API providers.
scenes.necessity: LLM API outages and rate limits occur frequently. Production architectures require dynamic routing and provider fallback.
scenes.story: Imagine an emergency room dispatch center. If the nearest hospital reaches 100% capacity or loses power, the dispatcher automatically reroutes incoming ambulances to a secondary hospital without stopping traffic.
scenes.narration:
Load Balancing और Multi-Provider Failover कैसे काम करता है?
सोचो तुम्हारी दुकान पर 1000 ग्राहक आ गए। अगर एक ही कैश काउंटर होगा तो लाइन लग जाएगी। Load Balancer ग्राहकों को 3 काउंटरों में बराबर बांट देता है।
और अगर एक काउंटर खराब हो जाए?
तो Load Balancer तुरंत समझ जाता है और नए ग्राहकों को बाकी दो काउंटरों पर भेज देता है। AI में ये OpenAI, Anthropic और Groq के बीच ट्रैफिक को बैलेंस करता है ताकि लेटेंसी सबसे कम रहे।
scenes.question: How do you design load balancing and routing across multiple model replicas or providers?
scenes.interview_question: How do you design load balancing and routing across multiple model replicas or providers?
scenes.interview_view:
Production LLM routers (e.g., LiteLLM, Portkey, custom gateways) sit between client applications and model providers. They enforce token-bucket rate limits, round-robin or least-latency load balancing across GPU replicas, and automatic failover fallback chains (e.g., primary OpenAI -> secondary Anthropic -> local vLLM). Circuit breakers prevent cascading failures by temporarily routing away from degraded endpoints.

Interview perspective:
Frame the answer as an engineering trade-off. Identify the latency/cost bottleneck, distinguish time-to-first-token from total latency and throughput, and discuss caching, batching, concurrency, timeouts, retries, rate limits, and graceful degradation where relevant.
interview_followups: What is the main bottleneck and how would you measure it?
How would your design behave under traffic spikes or provider throttling?
What would you optimize first if cost doubled without a quality change?

scenes.title: Implementing Exponential Backoff with Jitter for LLM APIs
scenes.teaching_intent: To teach resilient API retry patterns with randomized jitter to prevent thundering herd problems during rate limits.
scenes.necessity: Transient 429 and 503 errors are common when calling LLM APIs. Naive retry loops crash servers with synchronized retries.
scenes.story: If a door is temporarily locked and 100 people all try to turn the handle every exact 2 seconds, the door stays jammed. If everyone waits a random amount of time between 1 and 5 seconds, people slip through smoothly one by one.
scenes.narration:
Exponential Backoff with Jitter क्या है? जब API 'Rate Limit 429' फेंक दे तो क्या करें?
दोस्त, जब कोई सर्वर कहे 'रुक जाओ, बहुत भीड़ है', तो पागलों की तरह हर मिलीसेकंड पर दोबारा दरवाजा मत खटखटाओ, नहीं तो वो तुम्हें ब्लॉक कर देगा!
तो कितना इंतजार करें?
Exponential Backoff कहता है — पहले 1 सेकंड रुको, फिर 2 सेकंड, फिर 4 सेकंड, फिर 8 सेकंड! इंतजार का समय दोगुना करते जाओ।
और Jitter क्या है?
Jitter मतलब थोड़ा सा रैंडम समय जोड़ दो — जैसे 2.3 सेकंड या 3.8 सेकंड! ताकि सारे यूजर्स बिल्कुल एक ही मिलीसेकंड पर सर्वर पर दोबारा हमला न बोल दें। इसे कहते हैं समझदार इंजीनियरिंग!
scenes.question: How do you implement an exponential backoff retry wrapper with jitter for flaky LLM API calls?
scenes.interview_question: How do you implement an exponential backoff retry wrapper with jitter for flaky LLM API calls?
scenes.interview_view:
Exponential backoff increases wait time exponentially between retries (e.g., 1s, 2s, 4s, 8s). Full jitter adds a random delay between 0 and the exponential cap: sleep = random_uniform(0, min(max_delay, base_delay * 2^attempt)). This spreads out retries across client instances, preventing thundering herd spikes on rate-limited endpoints. Non-retryable errors (e.g., 400 Bad Request or 401 Unauthorized) should fail fast without retrying.

What would you optimize first if cost doubled without a quality change?

scenes.title: Token-Bucket Rate Limiter for LLM Applications
scenes.teaching_intent: To explain the mechanics of a token-bucket rate limiter algorithm for controlling outbound API request bursts and throughput.
scenes.necessity: LLM providers enforce Strict Requests-Per-Minute (RPM) and Tokens-Per-Minute (TPM). Rate limiters protect infrastructure from ban blocks.
scenes.story: Imagine an arcade machine that holds up to 10 tokens. Every second, 1 token drops into the coin slot automatically. You can spend 5 tokens at once in a quick burst, but once empty, you must wait for tokens to refill.
scenes.narration:
Token-Bucket Rate Limiter कैसे काम करता है?
सोचो एक बाल्टी है दोस्त, जिसमें ऊपर से हर सेकंड 10 पानी की बूंदें (टोकन्स) गिरती हैं। बाल्टी में ज्यादा से ज्यादा 100 बूंदें आ सकती हैं।
और जब कोई यूजर रिक्वेस्ट भेजता है?
तो वो बाल्टी में से 1 बूंद निकाल लेता है। अगर बाल्टी में पानी है, तो रिक्वेस्ट पास हो जाएगी। लेकिन अगर यूजर ने एक ही सेकंड में 200 रिक्वेस्ट भेज दीं, तो बाल्टी खाली हो जाएगी!
और बाकी रिक्वेस्ट्स को रोक दिया जाएगा?
हाँ, 'Rate Limit Exceeded'! जैसे ही बाल्टी में फिर से बूंदें भरेंगी, वो दोबारा रिक्वेस्ट कर सकता है। सबसे क्लासिक और असरदार तरीका!
scenes.question: How do you implement a token-bucket rate limiter for outgoing LLM API calls?
scenes.interview_question: How do you implement a token-bucket rate limiter for outgoing LLM API calls?
scenes.interview_view:
A token-bucket rate limiter tracks current token capacity up to a maximum bucket size. Tokens refill continuously over time: tokens = min(capacity, current_tokens + (now - last_refill) * refill_rate). When a request arrives, if tokens >= required_cost, tokens are decremented and the request proceeds; otherwise, the request is delayed or rejected. This allows short bursts up to capacity while strictly enforcing long-run average throughput.

What would you optimize first if cost doubled without a quality change?

scenes.title: Triage Scenario: Non-Deterministic Output Drift
scenes.teaching_intent: To provide a structured diagnostic methodology for debugging output drift in production LLM applications.
scenes.necessity: Users reporting different answers to identical prompts minutes apart indicates unconstrained sampling or dynamic prompt injection.
scenes.story: A user asks a support bot 'What is the refund policy?' at 10:00 AM and gets a clear 3-bullet summary. They ask the exact same question at 10:05 AM and get a vague 4-paragraph essay. What went wrong?
scenes.narration:
Triage Scenario — अचानक हमारे AI के जवाब अजीब होने लगे और drift आ गया! इसे कैसे ठीक करें?
घबराओ मत दोस्त! जब भी ऐसा हो, सबसे पहले 3 चीजें चेक करो: पहला — क्या किसी ने सिस्टम प्रॉम्प्ट में कोई नया शब्द जोड़ा है?
दूसरा क्या चेक करें?
क्या प्रोवाइडर ने मॉडल का वर्जन चुपचाप अपडेट कर दिया है? जैसे 'gpt-4o' के नीचे का स्नैपशॉट बदल गया हो। हमेशा 'gpt-4o-2024-08-06' जैसा फिक्स्ड पिन किया हुआ वर्जन यूज़ करो!
और तीसरा?
RAG के रिट्रीवल को देखो — क्या डेटाबेस में कोई नई फाइल आई है जो गलत सर्च रिजल्ट्स ला रही है? Traces देखने पर 5 मिनट में चोर पकड़ा जाएगा!
scenes.question: Users report that the chatbot gives noticeably different answers to the exact same question asked minutes apart. How do you debug this?
scenes.interview_question: Users report that the chatbot gives noticeably different answers to the exact same question asked minutes apart. How do you debug this?
scenes.interview_view:
Debugging non-deterministic drift requires auditing 4 primary variables: (1) Temperature setting — temperature > 0 introduces sampling variance; set temperature=0 for deterministic benchmarks. (2) Dynamic Context / RAG — verify if retrieved context chunks or timestamps changed between calls. (3) System Prompt / History — check if un-truncated chat history or dynamic system prompts are shifting. (4) Seed / Model Routing — check if multi-provider load balancers routed to different model snapshots (e.g., gpt-4o vs gpt-4o-mini).

Interview perspective:
A strong interview answer should define what is being measured, how the evaluation set is built, how regressions are detected, and how traces connect an incorrect answer to retrieval, model, tool, or application behavior. Mention human review where automated metrics are insufficient.
interview_followups: What would you put in an evaluation set before changing the system?
How would you distinguish model regression from retrieval or data regression?
What traces and metrics would you capture in production?

scenes.title: Triage Scenario: Exploding Monthly LLM API Spend
scenes.teaching_intent: To present cost-audit strategies for identifying and fixing runaway LLM token spend in live products.
scenes.necessity: LLM API spend can double or triple unexpectedly without traffic growth if prompt context or loop conditions balloon.
scenes.story: Your user base remained flat at 5,000 daily active users, but your monthly OpenAI invoice surged from $3,000 to $12,000. Where is the money leaking?
scenes.narration:
Triage Scenario — कंपनी का मंथली LLM बिल अचानक 3 गुना हो गया! आग कैसे बुझाएं?
तुरंत डैशबोर्ड खोलो दोस्त! सबसे पहले देखो कि क्या बिल इनपुट टोकन्स की वजह से बढ़ा या आउटपुट टोकन्स की वजह से?
अगर इनपुट टोकन्स की वजह से बढ़ा हो तो?
मतलब किसी ने RAG में बहुत बड़े-बड़े चंक्स भेजना शुरू कर दिया है, या चैट हिस्ट्री ट्रिम नहीं हो रही और 50 पुराने मैसेज हर बार भेजे जा रहे हैं!
और अगर आउटपुट टोकन्स की वजह से बढ़ा हो तो?

scenes.question: Monthly LLM API spend has tripled over three months while user traffic stayed flat. How do you investigate and fix it?
scenes.interview_question: Monthly LLM API spend has tripled over three months while user traffic stayed flat. How do you investigate and fix it?
scenes.interview_view:
Investigating LLM cost spikes requires token-level attribution: (1) Segment cost by input tokens vs. output tokens — input token growth points to ballooning context windows or RAG chunk sizes; output token growth points to verbose generation. (2) Check conversation history retention — unbounded chat histories re-sent on every turn cause exponential input token inflation. (3) Audit agent loops — check for looping agents making 20+ tool calls per turn. Fixes include prompt trimming, prompt caching (e.g., Anthropic/OpenAI prompt cache), exact-match semantic caching, and setting max_tokens caps.

scenes.title: System Design: Grounded Help-Center Chatbot
scenes.teaching_intent: To walk through an end-to-end production architecture for a grounded documentation assistant.
scenes.necessity: Building a production RAG chatbot requires integrating ingestion, vector search, re-ranking, guardrails, and analytics.
scenes.story: An enterprise wants an instant AI assistant for 50,000 help center articles. It must answer accurately, cite exact articles, and never leak internal confidential draft documents.
scenes.narration:
System Design — एक कंपनी के लिए 100% भरोसेमंद हेल्प-सेंटर चैटबॉट कैसे बनाएं?
दोस्त, इसका आर्किटेक्चर बहुत साफ होना चाहिए: सबसे आगे एक API Gateway और Rate Limiter। उसके पीछे Guardrails जो उल्टे-सीधे सवाल रोकें।
फिर बीच में क्या होगा?
बीच में Hybrid RAG Pipeline जो कंपनी के FAQs और नॉलेज बेस से सच निकाले। और एक Re-ranker जो सिर्फ टॉप 3 जवाब चुने।
और अगर बॉट को जवाब न मिले तब?
तो वो झूठ न बोले! एक कॉन्फिडेंस स्कोर तय करो। अगर स्कोर कम हो, तो चैट तुरंत एक असली इंसान (Human Support Agent) को ट्रांसफर हो जाए। कस्टमर भी खुश, कंपनी भी खुश!

scenes.key_takeaway: Design production RAG chatbots with automated document ingestion, hybrid search with re-ranking, strict guardrails, and real-time faithfulness tracing.

scenes.title: Narrating a RAG System Architecture End-to-End
scenes.teaching_intent: To teach candidates how to structure project walkthroughs highlighting trade-offs, engineering decisions, and quantitative evaluation.
scenes.necessity: Interviewers evaluate senior candidates on concrete architectural decisions, failures, and metrics rather than high-level tutorial summaries.
scenes.story: When asked 'Walk me through a RAG system you built,' saying 'I used LangChain and OpenAI' sounds like a beginner tutorial. Saying 'We processed 100k PDFs, used hybrid search with BGE-reranker, and improved faithfulness from 72% to 94%' proves production expertise.
scenes.narration:
इंटरव्यू में RAG सिस्टम का पूरा आर्किटेक्चर 2 मिनट में कैसे समझाएं?
कॉन्फिडेंस के साथ 3 ब्लॉक्स बताओ दोस्त: ब्लॉक 1 — Offline Ingestion Pipeline (डॉक्यूमेंट्स, चंकिंग, एम्बेडिंग्स और वेक्टर डेटाबेस)।
ब्लॉक 2 क्या है?
Online Retrieval Pipeline — जहाँ यूजर की क्वेरी को एम्बेड करके Hybrid Search (BM25 + Dense) करते हैं और Cross-Encoder से Re-rank करते हैं।
और ब्लॉक 3?
Generation & Guardrails — जहाँ ऑगमेंटेड प्रॉम्प्ट LLM को जाता है, स्ट्रीमिंग के जरिए जवाब आता है, और Faithfulness चेक करके यूजर को दिखाया जाता है। इंटरव्यूअर तुरंत इम्प्रेस हो जाएगा!
scenes.question: How do you walk through a RAG system you built end-to-end in an interview?
scenes.interview_question: How do you walk through a RAG system you built end-to-end in an interview?
scenes.interview_view:
Structure your project narrative around 4 key pillars: (1) Problem Context & Corpus Scale — describe document volume, update frequency, and domain challenges. (2) Architectural Choices & Trade-offs — justify chunk size, embedding model, vector DB selection, and why hybrid search or re-ranking was necessary. (3) Key Failure & Iteration — share a real production issue (e.g., table parsing failure, low precision) and how you solved it. (4) Quantitative Impact — state concrete metrics (e.g., latency reduction, cost savings, RAGAS faithfulness score improvement).

Interview perspective:
In an interview, do not stop at the definition. Explain where the failure can occur: query understanding, retrieval, re-ranking, context construction, generation, or post-processing. Discuss retrieval quality separately from answer quality, then mention evaluation, latency, freshness, and cost trade-offs.
interview_followups: How would you debug a RAG answer that is wrong: retrieval problem or generation problem?
Which metrics would you use to evaluate retrieval and final answer quality?
What production trade-off would make you choose a different approach?

scenes.title: Handling AI System Outage and Toxic Outputs
scenes.teaching_intent: To evaluate incident response, root-cause analysis, and mitigation when an AI application produces wrong or harmful outputs.
scenes.necessity: GenAI applications occasionally produce bad outputs. Showing structured incident resolution demonstrates engineering maturity.
scenes.story: A financial advisor AI bot tells a client to invest their life savings in a meme coin due to a hallucination. The client posts a screenshot on Twitter. What do you do in the first 60 minutes?
scenes.narration:
अगर AI सिस्टम बीच रात में टॉक्सिक या गलत जवाब देने लगे, तो क्या करें?
इमरजेंसी प्रोटोकॉल याद रखो दोस्त! स्टेप 1 — Containment! तुरंत अपने AI गेटवे से मॉडल का स्विच दबा दो और एक सेफ स्टैटिक मैसेज पर फॉलबैक कर दो। गलत बात बाहर नहीं जानी चाहिए!
स्टेप 2 क्या है?
Root Cause Analysis! रात के Traces खोलो — क्या किसी नए यूजर ने प्रॉम्प्ट इंजेक्शन किया? क्या कोई गंदा डॉक्यूमेंट डेटाबेस में चला गया?
और स्टेप 3?
Fix and Prevent! उस अटैक को अपने इवैल्यूएशन सूट में जोड़ो, गार्डरेल को अपडेट करो, और फिर नए टेस्ट पास होने के बाद ही सिस्टम दोबारा लाइव करो।
scenes.question: Tell me about a time an AI system you built produced a wrong or harmful output. What did you do?
scenes.interview_question: Tell me about a time an AI system you built produced a wrong or harmful output. What did you do?
scenes.interview_view:
Answer using the STAR-Incident framework: (1) Containment — immediately trigger guardrail blocks or fallback routing to mitigate ongoing risk. (2) Root Cause Analysis — trace the request telemetry log (input prompt, retrieved chunks, temperature, model version). (3) Structural Fix — ship regression test cases to the offline eval suite, update guardrail classifiers or prompt constraints. (4) Post-Mortem — document lessons learned and establish automated monitoring alerts to prevent recurrence.

Interview perspective:
Interviewers usually care about the application boundary, not only the model. Separate untrusted input from system instructions, validate tool arguments server-side, enforce least privilege, protect sensitive data, log safely, and define explicit refusal/fallback paths.
interview_followups: What is the main trade-off or limitation?
How would you apply this in a production system?
What failure mode would you watch for?

scenes.title: Resolving Technical Disagreements in GenAI Teams
scenes.teaching_intent: To demonstrate constructive technical collaboration, data-driven decision making, and alignment on team goals.
scenes.necessity: Engineers often disagree on architectures (e.g., Fine-tuning vs. RAG). Resolving disputes via empirical data shows leadership.
scenes.story: One senior engineer wants to spend 3 months fine-tuning a custom LLaMA model. Another wants to launch a simple RAG pipeline in 2 weeks. How do you resolve the deadlock?
scenes.narration:
जब AI टीम में दो इंजीनियर्स में बहस हो जाए — एक कहे 'फाइन-ट्यूनिंग करो', दूसरा कहे 'RAG करो' — तो फैसला कैसे करें?
दोस्त, बहस में कभी अपनी ईगो मत लाओ! इसे कहते हैं Data-Driven Decision Making। दोनों से कहो — 'बहस बंद करो, एक 100 सवालों का टेस्ट बेंचमार्क बनाओ!'
और दोनों तकनीकों को टेस्ट करो?
हाँ! एक इंजीनियर 3 दिन में RAG का प्रोटोटाइप बनाए, दूसरा छोटा LoRA मॉडल चलाए। फिर 4 चीजें नापो: Accuracy, Cost, Latency, और मेंटेनेंस का झंझट। जो डेटा में जीतेगा, वही प्रोडक्शन में जाएगा!
scenes.question: Tell me about a technical conflict you had with a teammate or manager and how you resolved it.
scenes.interview_question: Tell me about a technical conflict you had with a teammate or manager and how you resolved it.
scenes.interview_view:
Resolve technical disagreements empirically: (1) Define shared evaluation criteria — agree on target quality metrics, latency SLA, timeline, and budget. (2) Run a rapid prototype / benchmark — test both approaches on a representative dataset rather than arguing hypothetically. (3) Align on business outcomes — pick the option that satisfies immediate user needs while keeping architectural flexibility for future iterations.

Interview perspective:

interview_followups: What is the main trade-off or limitation?
How would you apply this in a production system?
What failure mode would you watch for?

scenes.title: The GenAI Master Glossary: Core Formulas & Terms
scenes.teaching_intent: To summarize foundational terms, formulas, and concepts for rapid interview review.
scenes.necessity: Quick-reference term mastery enables clear, concise communication during technical interview rounds.
scenes.story: Before walking into the interview room, you do a 2-minute mental scan of the core equations, model types, and key algorithms that form the bedrock of AI engineering.
scenes.narration:
Congratulations दोस्त! हम 78वें सीन पर पहुंच गए! चलो एक क्विक रिवीजन गेम खेलते हैं — AI के 3 सबसे बड़े फॉर्मूले!
चलो दक्ष, पहला फॉर्मूला बताओ!
Attention Formula — Softmax of (Q times K-transpose divided by square root of d-k) times V! ये है पूरे Transformer का दिल!
दूसरा फॉर्मूला?
LoRA Weight Update — W equals W-zero plus (B times A) times (alpha divided by r)! जहाँ विशालकाय मॉडल को छेड़े बिना छोटी मैट्रिक्स से ट्रेनिंग होती है!
और तीसरा फॉर्मूला?
Cosine Similarity — A dot B divided by (magnitude of A times magnitude of B)! जिससे दो शब्दों के बीच का मतलब और दूरी नापी जाती है। पूरा AI इंजीनियरिंग इन 3 फॉर्मूलों में समाया है!
scenes.question: What are the essential rapid-fire terms and formulas every GenAI engineer must know?
scenes.interview_question: What are the essential rapid-fire terms and formulas every GenAI engineer must know?
scenes.interview_view:
Core terms: (1) Scaled Dot-Product Attention: softmax(Query times Key-transpose / square root of d-k) V. (2) Decoder-Only: Causal attention, autoregressive text generation (GPT-4, LLaMA 3, Claude 3.5). (3) Encoder-Only: Bidirectional attention, representation learning (BERT). (4) KV Cache: Stores Key/Value tensors in GPU VRAM to avoid O(n^2) redundant computation during generation. (5) LoRA: Freezes pretrained weights and injects trainable low-rank rank-decomposition matrices (A and B). (6) DPO: Direct Preference Optimization without a separate reward model.

Interview perspective:
For interview depth, connect the mechanism to a concrete trade-off, failure mode, and production use case. Be ready to explain not only how it works, but when you would choose it and what you would monitor.
interview_followups: What is the main trade-off or limitation?
How would you apply this in a production system?
What failure mode would you watch for?

scenes.title: Context Engineering: Building the Right Context, Not Just the Right Prompt
scenes.teaching_intent: To distinguish prompt wording from the broader engineering problem of selecting, ordering, compressing, retrieving, validating, and updating the context supplied to an LLM.
scenes.necessity: Production LLM quality often depends on what information reaches the model, not just how the instruction is phrased.
scenes.story: A model can have a great prompt and still fail if the context contains stale documents, irrelevant chunks, noisy tool output, or too much history.
scenes.narration: प्रॉम्प्ट लिखना सिर्फ एक हिस्सा है। असली production सवाल है—मॉडल को कौन-सी जानकारी, किस क्रम में, कितनी मात्रा में और किस source से देनी है? इसी को Context Engineering के नजरिए से समझते हैं।
scenes.question: What is context engineering, and how is it different from prompt engineering?
scenes.interview_question: What is context engineering, and how is it different from prompt engineering?
scenes.interview_view:
Context engineering treats the model's full input as an engineered state: system instructions, user input, retrieved evidence, tool results, memory, constraints, and conversation history. The goal is to supply the right information in the right structure and order while controlling noise, token usage, freshness, and safety.

Interview perspective:
For interview depth, connect the mechanism to a concrete trade-off, failure mode, and production use case. Be ready to explain not only how it works, but when you would choose it and what you would monitor.
interview_followups: What is the main trade-off or limitation?
How would you apply this in a production system?
What failure mode would you watch for?

scenes.title: Model Context Protocol (MCP): Standardizing Model-to-Tool Connections
scenes.teaching_intent: To explain MCP as a standardized way for AI applications to discover and interact with external tools and data sources.
scenes.necessity: As agents connect to many tools, bespoke integrations become difficult to maintain, secure, and reuse.
scenes.story: Imagine every AI application inventing its own format for connecting to databases, files, APIs, and developer tools. MCP addresses this integration problem with a common protocol pattern.
scenes.narration: Function calling मॉडल को बताता है कि कौन-सा tool call करना है। MCP उससे आगे जाकर AI application और external tools तथा data के बीच connection को एक standard तरीके से organize करता है।
scenes.question: What is MCP, and how is it different from ordinary function calling?
scenes.interview_question: What is MCP, and how is it different from ordinary function calling?
scenes.interview_view:
MCP is an open protocol for connecting AI applications with external tools and data through standardized client-server interactions. Function calling describes how a model can request a tool; MCP standardizes more of the surrounding connection and discovery pattern. Production systems still need authentication, authorization, input/output validation, auditing, rate limits, and least-privilege access.

Interview perspective:
For a production answer, describe the control loop and boundaries: model decision, tool schema, authorization, execution, result validation, iteration limits, timeout/error handling, and observability. Also explain when a deterministic workflow is preferable to an agent.
interview_followups: When would you use a deterministic workflow instead of an agent?
How would you limit tool permissions and prevent unsafe actions?
How would you handle tool failure, loops, timeouts, and unexpected tool output?
scenes.production_angle: Permissions, validation, bounded execution, observability, failure recovery, and cost.

scenes.key_takeaway: MCP standardizes model-to-tool/data connectivity; it does not remove the need for application-level security and authorization.

scenes.title: Reliable LLM API Contracts: Structured Output Is Not Business Validation
scenes.teaching_intent: To teach the difference between schema-constrained output and actual application correctness.
scenes.necessity: A valid JSON object can still contain incorrect, unsafe, incomplete, or unauthorized values.
scenes.story: Suppose an LLM returns perfectly valid JSON with an account ID and refund amount. The JSON parser succeeds, but should your system immediately issue the refund? Definitely not.
scenes.narration: सिर्फ valid JSON मिल जाना मतलब जवाब सही है—ऐसा मानना खतरनाक है। Schema सिर्फ output का format validate करता है; business rules, correctness और authorization application को खुद enforce करने चाहिए।
scenes.question: If an LLM returns schema-valid structured output, what still needs to be validated?
scenes.interview_question: If an LLM returns schema-valid structured output, what still needs to be validated?
scenes.interview_view:

scenes.title: Agent vs. Workflow: When Not to Use an Agent
scenes.teaching_intent: To teach the architectural boundary between deterministic workflows and adaptive agents.
scenes.necessity: Using an agent where the steps are already known can add unnecessary latency, cost, nondeterminism, and security complexity.
scenes.story: If a task is always 'validate input → retrieve record → call API → format response', making an LLM decide every next step may create more problems than it solves.
scenes.narration: अगर workflow के steps पहले से तय हैं, तो हर जगह agent लगाना जरूरी नहीं है। Agent तब ज्यादा उपयोगी है जब अगला कदम runtime पर मिली information और tool results के आधार पर dynamically तय करना हो।
scenes.question: When should you use a deterministic workflow instead of an agent?
scenes.interview_question: When should you use a deterministic workflow instead of an agent?
scenes.interview_view:
Use a workflow when the sequence and branching logic are sufficiently known and can be represented explicitly. Use an agent when the next action depends materially on observations, tool results, or dynamic planning. Agents introduce additional model calls, failure modes, permissions, and nondeterminism, so they should earn their complexity.

Interview perspective:
For a production answer, describe the control loop and boundaries: model decision, tool schema, authorization, execution, result validation, iteration limits, timeout/error handling, and observability. Also explain when a deterministic workflow is preferable to an agent.
interview_followups: When would you use a deterministic workflow instead of an agent?
How would you limit tool permissions and prevent unsafe actions?
How would you handle tool failure, loops, timeouts, and unexpected tool output?

scenes.title: Production Debugging: The LLM System Is Wrong—Where Do You Start?
scenes.teaching_intent: To teach a systematic debugging approach for nondeterministic or multi-component LLM applications.
scenes.necessity: An incorrect answer can originate in input, retrieval, reranking, context construction, model generation, tools, post-processing, or business logic.
scenes.story: A user reports that the chatbot suddenly started giving wrong answers. Restarting the model is not a debugging strategy. First preserve the exact request and trace the complete execution path.
scenes.narration: LLM ने गलत जवाब दिया तो तुरंत model को दोष मत दो। पहले exact request, context, retrieval, tool calls, model version और output को capture करो; फिर पूरी pipeline को एक-एक stage पर isolate करके debug करो।
scenes.question: An LLM application suddenly produces wrong answers in production. How would you debug it?
scenes.interview_question: An LLM application suddenly produces wrong answers in production. How would you debug it?
scenes.interview_view:
First reproduce the request and preserve the relevant model/version, prompt, parameters, context, retrieved documents, reranker output, tool calls, tool results, and post-processing. Then isolate each stage: input/context, retrieval, generation, tools, and application logic. Compare against a known-good evaluation set and recent traces to identify regression, data drift, provider changes, or application bugs. Sensitive data in traces must be protected.

Interview perspective:
A strong interview answer should define what is being measured, how the evaluation set is built, how regressions are detected, and how traces connect an incorrect answer to retrieval, model, tool, or application behavior. Mention human review where automated metrics are insufficient.
interview_followups: What would you put in an evaluation set before changing the system?
How would you distinguish model regression from retrieval or data regression?
What traces and metrics would you capture in production?
